portzone.description: Call of Duty: Black Ops II Zombies and Multiplayer (BO2 Requiem), running natively on Switch with split-screen, online play, gyro aiming and a mod loader. Needs your own Black Ops II for PC from Steam.

notes: t6zm.nro starts Zombies and t6mp.nro Multiplayer directly; t6gameSW2.nro offers both. Start them from hbmenu.
Only the DLC maps you own are shown. The campaign isn't playable, so its files can stay on the PC.

inputs.label: Black Ops II for PC (Steam): the zone and sound folders from the game folder (the one with t6zm.exe), about 14.4 GB without the campaign

options.label: Copied from your Steam game folder

steps: Copy the zone and sound folders from your Steam game folder (the one with t6zm.exe) to switch/t6gameSW2/.
Or, on a PC, use the BO2 Requiem Compressor (https://hderick.github.io/BO2-Requiem-NX/) to shrink them first; choose Switch 2, and it makes a zip for the SD card's root.
Start t6gameSW2.nro from hbmenu.

notes: t6zm.nro starts Zombies and t6mp.nro Multiplayer directly; t6game.nro offers both.
Only the DLC maps you own are shown. The campaign isn't playable, so its files can stay on the PC.

inputs.label: Black Ops II for PC (Steam): the zone and sound folders from the game folder (the one with t6zm.exe), about 14.4 GB without the campaign

options.label: Copied from your Steam game folder

steps: Copy the zone and sound folders from your Steam game folder (the one with t6zm.exe) to switch/t6game/.
Or, on a PC, use the BO2 Requiem Compressor (https://hderick.github.io/BO2-Requiem-NX/) to shrink them first (down to 5.5 GB at Maximum, without the campaign); it makes a zip for the SD card's root.
Start t6game.nro with full memory: a forwarder, or hold R while starting a game.

portzone.description: Deus Ex on DX RUST, Grissyelda's ground-up rebuild of the game in Rust and Bevy, ported to Switch with bevy-horizon, with in-game updates. Needs your own Deus Ex: Game of the Year Edition for PC.

notes: The first launch compiles shaders as it meets them, so the first minutes stutter; later launches load them from the SD card.
Quitting returns to the HOME menu rather than the Homebrew Menu.
The game checks GitHub for a newer release a few seconds after it starts and offers it over the menu.

inputs.label: Deus Ex: Game of the Year Edition for PC, version 1.112fm

files.note: The folder holding System, Maps, Textures, Music and Sounds

generated.note: A record of each run; include it with bug reports
Optional test switches; a no_update_check line turns the update check off

steps: Copy your Deus Ex folder (the one holding System, Maps, Textures, Music and Sounds) to switch/dxview/DeusEx/.
Start dxview.nro with full memory: hold R while starting a game, or use a forwarder.

portzone.description: Halo: Combat Evolved from the decompilation, drawn with deko3d, with online play through OpenCE. Needs your own Xbox disc image.

notes: The game updates itself from its GitHub releases, asking first.

inputs.label: Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox disc image
Custom Edition maps

files.note: Sent by the host to players who lack them

prepare.summary: The first start copies the maps and movies out of the disc image, then starts the game.

generated.note: The game's icon, for a forwarder

steps: Make an image of your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox disc (.iso or .xiso).
Copy it to haloce-nx/ at the root of the SD card.
Start halo.nro with full memory. The first start copies the game data out of the image.

portzone.description: Horizon, Minecraft: Java Edition rewritten from scratch in Rust, ported to Switch, with splitscreen, Microsoft sign-in and in-game updates. Needs your own Minecraft: Java Edition, prepared on a PC.

notes: Graphics, Performance, Switch clocks raises the CPU, GPU and memory clocks; all are off by default and defer to sys-clk.

inputs.label: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 files, prepared by horizon-prepare (its horizon-prepare.json must say "output_version": 5)

files.note: The export's contents, with horizon-resources.json directly inside

prepare.summary: horizon-prepare, in every Horizon game Nightly archive (horizon-prepare.exe on Windows), makes the game's files from your own Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3.

steps: On a PC, prepare your own Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 with the latest horizon-prepare. Check that the export's horizon-prepare.json says "output_version": 5.
Copy the export's contents into switch/horizon/resources/, so horizon-resources.json sits directly inside it.
Start horizon.nro in application mode (a forwarder or title override), not from the Album.

portzone.description: Horizon, Minecraft: Java Edition rewritten in Rust, as a native Switch 2 build at 1080p and 120 Hz with Joy-Con 2 mouse controls. Needs your own Minecraft: Java Edition, prepared on a PC.

notes: Minus toggles the F3 debug screen; Options, Horizon Settings, Overlay shows the FPS and frame graph.
Joy-Con 2 mouse mode: the right Joy-Con points (R breaks, ZR places, the right stick picks a block) while the left stick walks.

inputs.label: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 files, prepared by the Horizon Launcher from your own copy

files.note: The prepared files, with horizon-resources.json directly inside

prepare.summary: The Horizon Launcher (PC or Mac) prepares the game's files from your own Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, into .local/horizon-client/26.3/.

steps: On a PC or Mac, prepare your own Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 with the Horizon Launcher.
Copy the contents of .local/horizon-client/26.3/ into switch/horizon/resources/, so horizon-resources.json sits directly inside it.
Start horizon.nro with Title Override: hold R while opening a native Switch 2 title.

portzone.description: Mario Kart Wii statically recompiled with WiiCompiled and KartPad, built on your PC from your disc into a launcher that also plays Retro Rewind. Needs your own Mario Kart Wii disc: PAL (RMCP01), first revision.

notes: Started from the Album it runs in low memory mode.
L + R3 opens the port menu: CPU boost and controller binds.
When Retro Rewind updates, build again and copy the new SD card folder; don't update RetroRewind6 on its own.

inputs.label: The SD card folder KartPadNX-Builder made from your Mario Kart Wii disc (PAL RMCP01, revision 0; .iso, .wbfs or .rvz), about 5 GB

files.note: The launcher, with the game built in

prepare.summary: KartPadNX-Builder (Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; about 15 GB free) reads your disc and builds the launcher with the game in it; the first build takes 30 to 60 minutes.

generated.note: Mods you add, one folder each; .zip files are unpacked by the launcher

steps: On a Windows PC, download KartPadNX-Builder.zip from the releases page, extract it and run KartPadNX-Builder.exe. Or use the web builder, https://kawaiibunga.github.io/KartPadNX/, which builds on the maintainer's PC.
Give it your Mario Kart Wii disc image (PAL RMCP01, revision 0). Other regions and revisions are rejected.
Copy the SD card folder it makes to the root of the SD card, or drop it on PortZone's upload page.
Hold R while starting a game, then start MKW Launcher.

portzone.description: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2, the PS2 version decompiled and ported natively to Switch, at 720p (1080p on Switch 2). Needs your own PS2 disc: the PAL version 1.00 (SLES-50731).

notes: Renders at 1080p. Start it from the ounce-hbmenu environment in full application mode.
The language is chosen at every start.
config.txt sets frame_limit (60 by default, up to 120) and show_fps.

Or, on a PC, give your unmodified ISO to the web installer (https://HDErick.github.io/NFSHP2_Switch_Port/) and choose Switch 2; it makes a zip for the SD card's root.
Start NFSHP2-Switch2.nro with full memory.

portzone.description: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005, Xbox 360), statically recompiled with ReXGlue and drawn with Vulkan on NVK: 30 FPS at stock clocks. Needs your own Xbox 360 disc, converted on a PC.

notes: A forwarder must be set to a 39-bit address space.
The first race after installing or updating can stutter for a few seconds while it compiles graphics pipelines; later sessions start smoothly.

inputs.label: Files made by the nfsmw-nx installer from your Xbox 360 disc

files.note: The game, the build for your disc's edition
The game's shaders, made from your disc

prepare.summary: The installer page reads your disc image (.iso) or extracted disc in the browser, picks your edition's build and makes the shaders from your disc.

steps: On a PC, open https://stevensnd.github.io/nfsmw-nx-installer/
Choose your disc image (.iso), or the folder with default.xex, Movies and NFS, and press Create nfsmw-nx.zip.
Extract nfsmw-nx.zip into switch/ on the SD card, or drop the extracted nfsmw-nx folder on PortZone's upload page. It makes switch/nfsmw-nx/.
Start nfsmw-nx.nro with full memory.

portzone.description: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) through OpenBLOPS, ported to Switch with Campaign, Zombies and Multiplayer. Needs your own PC copy, its zones converted on a PC.

notes: OpenBLOPS-NX2.nro runs Campaign and Zombies, OpenBLOPS-NX2-MP.nro Multiplayer; each can start the other.
Buttons go by position: A confirms and B goes back. Motion aiming is in Options, Controls, Gamepad.
cmdline.txt takes +set overrides.

notes: A forwarder must be set to a 39-bit address space.
Hold A+B+X+Y+L+R for the game menu.

portzone.description: Skate 3 Rust Engine, a Rust and Bevy skating game built from years of Skate 3 reverse-engineering research, ported to Switch with bevy-horizon, with in-game updates. Needs your own Skate 3 Xbox 360 disc, set up by the PC version.

notes: The first launch compiles shaders and keeps them in .mesa at the root of the SD card; each map's first launch builds its textures into cache/ (about 250 MB for University).
Plus opens the menu (graphics, difficulty, maps, character); the pause menu's Updates row installs new versions.

inputs.label: Files the PC version (experimental build 49) set up from your Skate 3 Xbox 360 disc, about 4.6 GB

options.label: Copied by switch_export.py, or by hand from the PC version's installation folder

prepare.summary: The Windows version sets the game up from your disc image (.iso) or extracted disc; switch_export.py from the Switch release zip then copies its files to the SD card.

generated.note: Textures built for the Switch, one map at a time; safe to delete
A record of each run, including updates
Optional rendering options; a no_update_check line stops the check at start-up

steps: On a PC, run skate3rust.exe from the Windows release, select your Skate 3 Xbox 360 ISO or default.xex, and let setup finish (it starts University). Then quit.
Run switch_export.py from the Switch release zip: python switch_export.py "<PC game folder>" <SD card>. It copies the game's files to switch/skate3rust/.
Start skate3rust.nro with full memory: hold R while starting a game.

portzone.description: Terraria, the PC version (FNA, .NET), built into a Switch homebrew on your PC by terrabuilder and run on Mono through mono-nx, ahead-of-time compiled. Needs your own Terraria for PC: GOG's Linux version.

notes: The NRO refuses applet mode (the Album) and says so.
Holding Plus and Minus together toggles the FPS counter.
The build's mono/ folder replaces sd:/mono/config.ini: if another mono-nx app uses one, back it up first.

files.note: The game, built from your copy

prepare.summary: terrabuilder (Windows through WSL, or Linux) builds the game from the Terraria folder you give it; the build lands in Output/Terraria/sdcard.

generated.note: Your characters, worlds and settings; a new build leaves them alone

steps: On a PC, download terrabuilder.cmd (Windows) or terrabuilder.sh (Linux) from the builder release into an empty folder and run it.
Put your Terraria (GOG 1.4.5.8 for Linux: its game folder or the whole GOG install) in the Terraria folder it makes, and choose Terraria (vanilla).
Copy everything inside Output/Terraria/sdcard to the root of the SD card, or drop the sdcard folder on PortZone's upload page.
Start Terraria.nro with full memory: hold R while starting a game.

portzone.description: tModLoader with your choice of mods, built into a Switch homebrew on your PC by terrabuilder with the mods compiled in, running on Mono through mono-nx. Experimental. Needs your own Terraria for PC (GOG or Steam).

notes: The NRO and the mods beside it are a matched pair: install the whole build each time, and don't update its mods from the in-game Mod Browser.
The NRO refuses applet mode (the Album) and says so.
Plus opens and closes the full-screen map.

inputs.label: The tModLoader build terrabuilder made from your Terraria (1.4.4.9 or 1.4.5.x Content folder): Output/tModLoader/sdcard

files.note: The mods built in, and your saves

prepare.summary: terrabuilder (Windows through WSL, or Linux) builds tModLoader and the mods you pick from your Terraria's Content folder; the first build takes about an hour, and lands in Output/tModLoader/sdcard.

steps: On a PC, download terrabuilder.cmd (Windows) or terrabuilder.sh (Linux) from the builder release into an empty folder and run it.
Put your Terraria (its Content folder from 1.4.4.9 or 1.4.5.x, GOG or Steam) in the Terraria folder it makes, any .tmod files in Mods, and choose tModLoader.
Copy everything inside Output/tModLoader/sdcard to the root of the SD card, overwriting what is there, or drop the sdcard folder on PortZone's upload page.
Start tmodloader.nro with full memory: hold R while starting a game.

Press both sticks in (L3+R3) for settings, the performance overlay and updates.

portzone.description: Ultimate Spider-Man (2005), the PC version statically recompiled to run natively on Switch, with an overlay for graphics, controls and performance. Needs your own PC copy: USM.exe and its Data folder.

notes: Minus, or L+R+Plus, opens the overlay: graphics, controls (swap A/B), performance (FPS cap, clocks) and Save settings to SD.
720p handheld runs at 30 FPS at stock clocks; 1080p docked needs the overlay's overclock. A resolution change needs Save settings to SD and a restart.
